texts.orig: · Do not rest your foot on the brake pedal while driving.
texts.text: Do not rest your foot on the brake pedal while driving.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Keep the wheels in correct alignment.
texts.text: Keep the wheels in correct alignment.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Keep windows closed at high speeds.
texts.text: Keep windows closed at high speeds.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Slow down when driving in crosswinds and headwinds.
texts.text: Slow down when driving in crosswinds and headwinds.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Never stop the engine when going down a hill
texts.text: Never stop the engine when going down a hill

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Stopping the engine when going down a hill is dangerous. This causes the loss of power steering and power brake control, and may cause damage to the drivetrain. Any loss of steering or braking control could cause an accident.
texts.text: Stopping the engine when going down a hill is dangerous. This causes the loss of power steering and power brake control, and may cause damage to the drivetrain. Any loss of steering or braking control could cause an accident.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: When driving on ice or in water, snow, mud, sand, or similar hazards:
texts.text: When driving on ice or in water, snow, mud, sand, or similar hazards:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Be cautious and allow extra distance for braking.
texts.text: Be cautious and allow extra distance for braking.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Avoid sudden braking and sudden maneuvering.
texts.text: Avoid sudden braking and sudden maneuvering.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Do  not  pump  the  brakes.  Continue  to  press  down  on  the  brake pedal. Refer to Antilock Brake System (ABS) on P. 215.
texts.text: Do  not  pump  the  brakes.  Continue  to  press  down  on  the  brake pedal. Refer to Antilock Brake System (ABS) on P. 215.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · If you get stuck, select a lower gear and accelerate slowly. Do not spin the front wheels.
texts.text: If you get stuck, select a lower gear and accelerate slowly. Do not spin the front wheels.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · For  more  traction  in  starting  on  slippery  surfaces  such  as  ice  or packed snow, use sand, rock salt, chains, carpeting, or other nonslip material under the front wheels.
texts.text: For  more  traction  in  starting  on  slippery  surfaces  such  as  ice  or packed snow, use sand, rock salt, chains, carpeting, or other nonslip material under the front wheels.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Use snow chains only on the front wheels.
texts.text: Use snow chains only on the front wheels.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: ■ Be extremely careful  if  it  is  necessary  to  downshift  on  slippery  surfaces
texts.text: ■ Be extremely careful  if  it  is  necessary  to  downshift  on  slippery  surfaces

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Downshifting into lower gear while driving on slippery surfaces is dangerous. The sudden change in tire speed could cause the tires to skid. This could lead to loss of vehicle control and an accident.
texts.text: Downshifting into lower gear while driving on slippery surfaces is dangerous. The sudden change in tire speed could cause the tires to skid. This could lead to loss of vehicle control and an accident.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Use  only  floor  mats  designed  specifically  for  vehicles  of  the same model and model year as your vehicle.
texts.text: Use  only  floor  mats  designed  specifically  for  vehicles  of  the same model and model year as your vehicle.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: When setting a floor mat, position the floor mat so that its grommets are inserted over the pointed end of the retention posts.
texts.text: When setting a floor mat, position the floor mat so that its grommets are inserted over the pointed end of the retention posts.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: ■ Make sure the floor mats are hooked on the retention pins to prevent them from bunching up under the foot pedals
texts.text: ■ Make sure the floor mats are hooked on the retention pins to prevent them from bunching up under the foot pedals

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Using a floor mat that is not secured is dangerous as it will interfere with the accelerator and brake pedal operation, which could result in an accident.
texts.text: Using a floor mat that is not secured is dangerous as it will interfere with the accelerator and brake pedal operation, which could result in an accident.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: ■ Do not install two floor mats, one on top of the other, on the driver's side
texts.text: ■ Do not install two floor mats, one on top of the other, on the driver's side

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Installing two floor mats, one on top of the other, on the driver's side is dangerous as the retention pins can only keep one floor mat from sliding forward.
texts.text: Installing two floor mats, one on top of the other, on the driver's side is dangerous as the retention pins can only keep one floor mat from sliding forward.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: If using an all weather mat for winter use always remove the original floor mat.
texts.text: If using an all weather mat for winter use always remove the original floor mat.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Loose floor mat(s) will interfere with the foot pedal and could result in an accident.
texts.text: Loose floor mat(s) will interfere with the foot pedal and could result in an accident.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: If you must rock the vehicle to free it from snow, sand or mud, depress the accelerator slightly and slowly move the shift lever from 1 (D) to R position.
texts.text: If you must rock the vehicle to free it from snow, sand or mud, depress the accelerator slightly and slowly move the shift lever from 1 (D) to R position.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: ■ Do not spin  the  wheels  at  more  than  35  mph  (56  km/h),  and  do  not allow anyone to stand behind a wheel when pushing the vehicle
texts.text: ■ Do not spin  the  wheels  at  more  than  35  mph  (56  km/h),  and  do  not allow anyone to stand behind a wheel when pushing the vehicle

texts.label: text
texts.orig: When the vehicle is stuck, spinning the wheels at high speed is dangerous. The  spinning  tire  could  overheat  and  explode.  This  could  cause  serious injuries.
texts.text: When the vehicle is stuck, spinning the wheels at high speed is dangerous. The  spinning  tire  could  overheat  and  explode.  This  could  cause  serious injuries.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Too much rocking may cause engine overheating, transaxle failure, and tire damage.
texts.text: Too much rocking may cause engine overheating, transaxle failure, and tire damage.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Carry emergency gear, including tire chains, window scraper, flares, a small shovel, jumper cables, and a small bag of sand or salt.
texts.text: Carry emergency gear, including tire chains, window scraper, flares, a small shovel, jumper cables, and a small bag of sand or salt.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Ask your Toyota dealer to check the following:
texts.text: Ask your Toyota dealer to check the following:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Have the proper ratio of antifreeze in the radiator. Refer to Engine Coolant on P. 398.
texts.text: Have the proper ratio of antifreeze in the radiator. Refer to Engine Coolant on P. 398.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Inspect the battery and its cables. Cold reduces battery capacity.
texts.text: Inspect the battery and its cables. Cold reduces battery capacity.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Use an engine oil appropriate for the lowest ambient temperatures that the vehicle will be driven in (  P. 395).
texts.text: Use an engine oil appropriate for the lowest ambient temperatures that the vehicle will be driven in (  P. 395).

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Inspect the ignition system for damage and loose connections.
texts.text: Inspect the ignition system for damage and loose connections.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Use washer fluid made with antifreeze  but do not use engine coolant antifreeze for washer fluid (  P. 402).
texts.text: Use washer fluid made with antifreeze  but do not use engine coolant antifreeze for washer fluid (  P. 402).

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: ● Do not use the parking brake in freezing weather as it may freeze. Instead, shift to 1 or R with a manual transaxle and to P with an automatic transaxle. Block the rear wheels.
texts.text: Do not use the parking brake in freezing weather as it may freeze. Instead, shift to 1 or R with a manual transaxle and to P with an automatic transaxle. Block the rear wheels.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: ● Remove snow before driving. Snow left on the windshield is dangerous as it could obstruct vision.
texts.text: Remove snow before driving. Snow left on the windshield is dangerous as it could obstruct vision.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: ● Do not apply excessive force to a window scraper when removing ice or frozen snow on the mirror glass and windshield.
texts.text: Do not apply excessive force to a window scraper when removing ice or frozen snow on the mirror glass and windshield.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: ● Never use warm or hot water for removing snow or ice from windows and mirrors as it could result in the glass cracking.
texts.text: Never use warm or hot water for removing snow or ice from windows and mirrors as it could result in the glass cracking.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: ● Drive slowly. Braking performance can be adversely affected if snow or ice adheres to the brake components. If this situation occurs, drive the vehicle slowly, releasing the accelerator pedal and lightly applying the brakes several times until the brake performance returns to normal.
texts.text: Drive slowly. Braking performance can be adversely affected if snow or ice adheres to the brake components. If this situation occurs, drive the vehicle slowly, releasing the accelerator pedal and lightly applying the brakes several times until the brake performance returns to normal.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: ■ Use snow tires on all four wheels
texts.text: ■ Use snow tires on all four wheels

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Do not go faster than 75 mph (120 km/h) while driving with snow tires. Inflate snow tires 30 kPa (0.3 kgf/cm 2 , 4.3 psi) more than recommended  on  the  tire  pressure  label  (driver's  door  frame),  but never  more  than  the  maximum  cold-tire  pressure  shown  on  the tires.
texts.text: Do not go faster than 75 mph (120 km/h) while driving with snow tires. Inflate snow tires 30 kPa (0.3 kgf/cm 2 , 4.3 psi) more than recommended  on  the  tire  pressure  label  (driver's  door  frame),  but never  more  than  the  maximum  cold-tire  pressure  shown  on  the tires.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The vehicle is originally equipped with all season radials designed to be used all year around. In some extreme climates you may find it  necessary  to  replace  them  with  snow  tires  during  the  winter months to further improve traction on snow and ice covered roads.
texts.text: The vehicle is originally equipped with all season radials designed to be used all year around. In some extreme climates you may find it  necessary  to  replace  them  with  snow  tires  during  the  winter months to further improve traction on snow and ice covered roads.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: ■ Use only the same size and type tires (snow, radial, or non-radial) on all four wheels
texts.text: ■ Use only the same size and type tires (snow, radial, or non-radial) on all four wheels

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Using tires different in size or type is dangerous. Your vehicle's handling could be greatly affected and result in an accident.
texts.text: Using tires different in size or type is dangerous. Your vehicle's handling could be greatly affected and result in an accident.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Check local regulations before using studded tires.
texts.text: Check local regulations before using studded tires.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Check local regulations before using tire chains.
texts.text: Check local regulations before using tire chains.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Install the chains on the front tires only.
texts.text: Install the chains on the front tires only.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Do not use chains on the rear tires.
texts.text: Do not use chains on the rear tires.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: If your vehicle is equipped with wheel covers remove them, otherwise the chain bands will scratch them. 1
texts.text: If your vehicle is equipped with wheel covers remove them, otherwise the chain bands will scratch them. 1

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Secure the chains on the front tires as tightly as possible. Always follow the chain manufacturer's instructions. 2
texts.text: Secure the chains on the front tires as tightly as possible. Always follow the chain manufacturer's instructions. 2

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Retighten the chains after driving 1/4-1/2 mile (1/2-1 km). 3
texts.text: Retighten the chains after driving 1/4-1/2 mile (1/2-1 km). 3

texts.label: text
texts.orig: If your vehicle is equipped with the tire pressure monitoring system, the system may not function correctly when using tire chains.
texts.text: If your vehicle is equipped with the tire pressure monitoring system, the system may not function correctly when using tire chains.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: ● Do not go faster than 30 mph (50 km/h) or the chain manufacturer's recommended limit, whichever is lower.
texts.text: Do not go faster than 30 mph (50 km/h) or the chain manufacturer's recommended limit, whichever is lower.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: ● Drive carefully and avoid bumps, holes, and sharp turns.
texts.text: Drive carefully and avoid bumps, holes, and sharp turns.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: ● Do not use chains on a temporary spare tire; it may result in damage to the vehicle and to the tire.
texts.text: Do not use chains on a temporary spare tire; it may result in damage to the vehicle and to the tire.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: ● Do not use chains on roads that are free of snow or ice. The tires and chains could be damaged.
texts.text: Do not use chains on roads that are free of snow or ice. The tires and chains could be damaged.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: ● Chains may scratch or chip aluminum wheels.
texts.text: Chains may scratch or chip aluminum wheels.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: ■ Dry off brakes that have become wet by driving slowly, releasing the accelerator  pedal  and  lightly  applying  the  brakes  several  times  until the brake performance returns to normal
texts.text: ■ Dry off brakes that have become wet by driving slowly, releasing the accelerator  pedal  and  lightly  applying  the  brakes  several  times  until the brake performance returns to normal

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Driving with wet brakes is dangerous. Increased stopping distance or the vehicle pulling to one side when braking could result in a serious accident. Light braking will indicate whether the brakes have been affected.
texts.text: Driving with wet brakes is dangerous. Increased stopping distance or the vehicle pulling to one side when braking could result in a serious accident. Light braking will indicate whether the brakes have been affected.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Do not drive the vehicle on flooded roads as it could cause short circuiting of  electrical/electronic  parts,  or  engine  damage  or  stalling  from  water absorption. If the vehicle has been immersed in water, consult your Toyota dealer.
texts.text: Do not drive the vehicle on flooded roads as it could cause short circuiting of  electrical/electronic  parts,  or  engine  damage  or  stalling  from  water absorption. If the vehicle has been immersed in water, consult your Toyota dealer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: ■ Be careful not to overload your vehicle
texts.text: ■ Be careful not to overload your vehicle

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The gross axle weight rating (GAWR) and the gross vehicle weight rating  (GVWR) of the vehicle are on the Motor Vehicle Safety Standard Label on the driver's door frame. Exceeding these ratings can cause an accident or vehicle damage. You can estimate the weight of the load by weighing the items (or people) before putting them in the vehicle.
texts.text: The gross axle weight rating (GAWR) and the gross vehicle weight rating  (GVWR) of the vehicle are on the Motor Vehicle Safety Standard Label on the driver's door frame. Exceeding these ratings can cause an accident or vehicle damage. You can estimate the weight of the load by weighing the items (or people) before putting them in the vehicle.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Your  vehicle's  suspension  and  underbody  can  be  damaged  if driven on rough/uneven roads or over speed bumps at excessive  speeds.  Use  care  and  reduce  speed  when  traveling  on rough/uneven roads or over speed bumps.
texts.text: Your  vehicle's  suspension  and  underbody  can  be  damaged  if driven on rough/uneven roads or over speed bumps at excessive  speeds.  Use  care  and  reduce  speed  when  traveling  on rough/uneven roads or over speed bumps.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Use care not to damage the vehicle's underbody, bumpers or muffler(s) when driving under the following conditions:
texts.text: Use care not to damage the vehicle's underbody, bumpers or muffler(s) when driving under the following conditions:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Ascending or descending a slope with a sharp transition angle
texts.text: Ascending or descending a slope with a sharp transition angle

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Ascending or descending a driveway or trailer ramp with a sharp transition angle
texts.text: Ascending or descending a driveway or trailer ramp with a sharp transition angle

texts.label: text
texts.orig: This vehicle is equipped with low profile tires allowing class-leading performance and handling. As a result, the sidewall of the tires are very thin and the  tires  and  wheels  can  be  damaged  if  driven  through  potholes  or  on rough/uneven  roads  at  excessive  speeds.  Use  care  and  reduce  speed when traveling on rough/uneven roads or through potholes.
texts.text: This vehicle is equipped with low profile tires allowing class-leading performance and handling. As a result, the sidewall of the tires are very thin and the  tires  and  wheels  can  be  damaged  if  driven  through  potholes  or  on rough/uneven  roads  at  excessive  speeds.  Use  care  and  reduce  speed when traveling on rough/uneven roads or through potholes.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Your Toyota is not designed for towing. Never tow a trailer with your Toyota.
texts.text: Your Toyota is not designed for towing. Never tow a trailer with your Toyota.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: An  example  of  'recreational  towing'  is  towing  your  vehicle behind a motorhome.
texts.text: An  example  of  'recreational  towing'  is  towing  your  vehicle behind a motorhome.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The  transaxle  is  not  designed  for  towing  this  vehicle  on  all  4 wheels.
texts.text: The  transaxle  is  not  designed  for  towing  this  vehicle  on  all  4 wheels.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: When doing recreational towing refer to 'Towing Description' (  P. 486) and 'Tiedown Hooks' (  P. 487) and carefully follow the instructions.
texts.text: When doing recreational towing refer to 'Towing Description' (  P. 486) and 'Tiedown Hooks' (  P. 487) and carefully follow the instructions.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The system operates only when the driver is in the vehicle or within operational range while the key is being carried.
texts.text: The system operates only when the driver is in the vehicle or within operational range while the key is being carried.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Each time the push button start is pressed,  the  ignition  switches  in the  order  of  off,  ACC,  and  ON. Pressing  the push  button start again from ON switches the ignition off.
texts.text: Each time the push button start is pressed,  the  ignition  switches  in the  order  of  off,  ACC,  and  ON. Pressing  the push  button start again from ON switches the ignition off.

texts.text: The power supply to electrical devices turns off and the push button start indicator light (amber) also turns off.

texts.label: text

texts.text: In this position the steering wheel is locked.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Some  electrical  accessories  will  operate  and  the  indicator  light (amber) illuminates.
texts.text: Some  electrical  accessories  will  operate  and  the  indicator  light (amber) illuminates.

texts.label: text

texts.text: This is the normal running position after the engine is started. The indicator light (amber) turns off. (The indicator light (amber) illuminates when the ignition is switched ON and the engine is not running.)

texts.label: text

texts.text: Some indicator lights/warning lights should be inspected before the engine is started (  P. 173).

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: ● The engine starts by pressing the push button start while depressing the clutch pedal (manual transaxle) or the brake pedal (automatic transaxle). To switch the ignition position, press the push button start without depressing the pedal.
texts.text: The engine starts by pressing the push button start while depressing the clutch pedal (manual transaxle) or the brake pedal (automatic transaxle). To switch the ignition position, press the push button start without depressing the pedal.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: ● Do not leave the ignition switched ON while the engine is not running. Doing so could result in the battery going dead. If the ignition is left in ACC (For automatic transaxle, the selector lever is in the P position, and the ignition is in ACC), the ignition switches off automatically after about 25 minutes.
texts.text: Do not leave the ignition switched ON while the engine is not running. Doing so could result in the battery going dead. If the ignition is left in ACC (For automatic transaxle, the selector lever is in the P position, and the ignition is in ACC), the ignition switches off automatically after about 25 minutes.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The keyless entry system does not function while the push button start has been pressed to ACC, and the doors will not lock/unlock even if they have been locked manually.
texts.text: The keyless entry system does not function while the push button start has been pressed to ACC, and the doors will not lock/unlock even if they have been locked manually.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: When the push button start is pressed to ON, the sound of the fuel pump motor operating near the fuel tank can be heard. This does not indicate an abnormality.
texts.text: When the push button start is pressed to ON, the sound of the fuel pump motor operating near the fuel tank can be heard. This does not indicate an abnormality.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: ■ Before leaving the driver's seat, set the parking brake, make sure the selector lever is in 1st gear or R (manual transaxle) or in P (automatic transaxle), and always switch the ignition off
texts.text: ■ Before leaving the driver's seat, set the parking brake, make sure the selector lever is in 1st gear or R (manual transaxle) or in P (automatic transaxle), and always switch the ignition off

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Leaving  the  driver's  seat  without  setting  the  parking  brake,  shifting  the selector lever to 1st gear or R (manual transaxle) or to P (automatic transaxle),  and  switching  the  ignition  off  is  dangerous.  Unexpected  vehicle movement could occur which could result in an accident.
texts.text: Leaving  the  driver's  seat  without  setting  the  parking  brake,  shifting  the selector lever to 1st gear or R (manual transaxle) or to P (automatic transaxle),  and  switching  the  ignition  off  is  dangerous.  Unexpected  vehicle movement could occur which could result in an accident.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In addition, if your intention is to leave the vehicle for even a short period, it is important to switch the ignition off, as leaving it in another position will disable some of the vehicle's security systems and run the battery down.
texts.text: In addition, if your intention is to leave the vehicle for even a short period, it is important to switch the ignition off, as leaving it in another position will disable some of the vehicle's security systems and run the battery down.

texts.text: If  the  push  button  start  indicator light  (green)  flashes  with  the  key being carried, touch the key to the push  button  start and  start  the engine. Refer to Engine Start Function When Key Battery is Dead on P. 161.

When  the  driver releases  the  brake  pedal  and  depresses  the  accelerator  pedal while on a slope, the function prevents the vehicle from rolling. The  braking  force  is  maintained  automatically  after  the  brake pedal is released on a steep grade.
texts.text: Hill Launch Assist (HLA) is a function which assists the driver in accelerating  from  a  stop  while  on  a  slope.  When  the  driver releases  the  brake  pedal  and  depresses  the  accelerator  pedal while on a slope, the function prevents the vehicle from rolling. The  braking  force  is  maintained  automatically  after  the  brake pedal is released on a steep grade.

texts.text: For vehicles with a manual transaxle, Hill Launch Assist (HLA) operates on a downward slope when the shift lever is in the reverse (R) position, and on an upward slope when the shift lever is in a position other than the reverse (R) position.

texts.orig: Please note that the TPMS is not a substitute for proper tire maintenance, and it is the driver's responsibility to maintain correct tire pressure,  even  if  under-inflation  has  not  reached  the  level  to  trigger illumination of the TPMS low tire pressure telltale.
texts.text: Please note that the TPMS is not a substitute for proper tire maintenance, and it is the driver's responsibility to maintain correct tire pressure,  even  if  under-inflation  has  not  reached  the  level  to  trigger illumination of the TPMS low tire pressure telltale.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: As an added safety feature, your vehicle has been equipped with a tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS) that illuminates a low tire pressure  telltale  when  one  or  more  of  your  tires  is  significantly  underinflated. Accordingly,  when  the  low  tire  pressure  telltale  illuminates, you should stop and check your tires as soon as possible, and inflate them to the proper pressure. Driving on a significantly under-inflated tire causes the tire to overheat and can lead to tire failure. Under-inflation also reduces fuel efficiency and tire tread life, and may affect the vehicle's handling and stopping ability.
texts.text: As an added safety feature, your vehicle has been equipped with a tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS) that illuminates a low tire pressure  telltale  when  one  or  more  of  your  tires  is  significantly  underinflated. Driving on a significantly under-inflated tire causes the tire to overheat and can lead to tire failure. Under-inflation also reduces fuel efficiency and tire tread life, and may affect the vehicle's handling and stopping ability.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Your vehicle has also been equipped with a TPMS malfunction indicator to indicate when the system is not operating properly.
texts.text: Your vehicle has also been equipped with a TPMS malfunction indicator to indicate when the system is not operating properly.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The TPMS malfunction indicator is combined with the low tire pressure telltale. When the system detects a malfunction, the telltale will flash for  approximately  one  minute  and  then  remain  continuously  illuminated. This sequence will continue upon subsequent vehicle start-ups as long as the malfunction exists. When the malfunction indicator is illuminated,  the  system  may  not  be  able  to  detect  or  signal  low  tire pressure as intended. TPMS malfunctions may occur for a variety of reasons, including the installation of replacement or alternate tires or wheels on the vehicle that prevent the TPMS from functioning properly. Always  check  the  TPMS  malfunction  telltale  after  replacing  one  or more tires or wheels on your vehicle to ensure that the replacement or alternate tires and wheels allow the TPMS to continue to function properly.

texts.orig: Signals  from  an  FM  transmitter  are  similar  to  beams  of  light because  they  do  not  bend  around  corners,  but  they  do  reflect. texts.label: text
texts.orig: HD Radio™ Technology is the digital evolution of analog AM/FM radio. Your radio product has a special receiver which allows it to receive  digital  broadcasts  (where  available)  in  addition  to  the analog  broadcasts  it  already  receives. For  more  information,  and  a guide to available radio stations and programming, please visit www.hdradio.com.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: ■ Etching Caused by Acid Rain or Industrial Fallout
texts.text: ■ Etching Caused by Acid Rain or Industrial Fallout

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Industrial pollutants and vehicle emissions drift into the air and mix with rain or dew to form acids. These acids can settle on a vehicle's finish. As the water evaporates, the acid becomes concentrated and can damage the finish.
texts.text: Industrial pollutants and vehicle emissions drift into the air and mix with rain or dew to form acids. These acids can settle on a vehicle's finish. As the water evaporates, the acid becomes concentrated and can damage the finish.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: And the longer the acid remains on the surface, the greater the chance is for damage.
texts.text: And the longer the acid remains on the surface, the greater the chance is for damage.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: It is necessary to wash and wax your vehicle to preserve its finish according to the instructions in this section. These steps should be taken immediately after you suspect that acid rain has settled on your vehicle's finish.
texts.text: It is necessary to wash and wax your vehicle to preserve its finish according to the instructions in this section. These steps should be taken immediately after you suspect that acid rain has settled on your vehicle's finish.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Damage Caused by Bird Dropping, Insects, or Tree Sap
texts.text: Damage Caused by Bird Dropping, Insects, or Tree Sap

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Bird droppings contain acids. If these are not removed they can eat away the clear and color base coat of the vehicle's paintwork.
texts.text: Bird droppings contain acids. If these are not removed they can eat away the clear and color base coat of the vehicle's paintwork.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: When insects stick to the paint surface and decompose, corrosive compounds form.
texts.text: When insects stick to the paint surface and decompose, corrosive compounds form.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: These can erode the clear and color base coat of the vehicle's paintwork if they are not removed.
texts.text: These can erode the clear and color base coat of the vehicle's paintwork if they are not removed.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Tree sap will harden and adhere permanently to the paint finish. If you scratch the sap off while it is hard, some vehicle paint could come off with it.
texts.text: Tree sap will harden and adhere permanently to the paint finish. If you scratch the sap off while it is hard, some vehicle paint could come off with it.

texts.label: text

texts.text: It  is  necessary to have your Toyota washed and waxed to preserve its finish according to the instructions in this section. This should be done as soon as possible.

texts.orig: Bird droppings can be removed with a soft sponge and water. If you are traveling and these are not available, a moistened tissue may also take care of the problem. The cleaned area should be waxed according to the instructions in this section.
texts.text: Bird droppings can be removed with a soft sponge and water. If you are traveling and these are not available, a moistened tissue may also take care of the problem. The cleaned area should be waxed according to the instructions in this section.

texts.text: Another  method  is  to  cover  the  affected  area  with  dampened newspaper for 1 to 2 hours. After removing the newspaper, rinse off the loosened debris with water.

texts.text: Paint chipping occurs when gravel thrown in the air by another vehicle's tires hits your vehicle.

texts.label: text

texts.text: Keeping  a  safe  distance  between  you  and  the  vehicle  ahead reduces  the  chances  of  having  your  paint  chipped  by  flying gravel.

texts.label: text

If the car washer nozzle is  put  too  close  to  the  vehicle,  the  force  of  the spray could damage or deform the molding, affect the sealability of parts, and allow water to penetrate the interior. Keep a sufficient space (12 in. (300 mm) or more) between the nozzle and the vehicle. In addition, do not spend too much time spraying the same  area  of  the  vehicle,  and  be  very  careful  when  spraying between gaps in doors and around windows.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: ● Perform tire pressure adjustment when the tires are cold. Tire pressure will vary according to the tire temperature, therefore let the vehicle stand for 1 hour or only drive it 1 mile (1.6 km) or less before adjusting the tire pressures. When pressure is adjusted on hot tires to the cold inflation pressure, the TPMS warning light/beep may turn on after the tires cool and pressure drops below specification.
texts.text: Perform tire pressure adjustment when the tires are cold. Tire pressure will vary according to the tire temperature, therefore let the vehicle stand for 1 hour or only drive it 1 mile (1.6 km) or less before adjusting the tire pressures. When pressure is adjusted on hot tires to the cold inflation pressure, the TPMS warning light/beep may turn on after the tires cool and pressure drops below specification.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Also, an illuminated TPMS warning light, resulting from the tire air pressure dropping due to cold ambient temperature will remain illuminated even if the ambient temperature rises. In this case, it will also be necessary to adjust the tire air pressures. If the TPMS warning light illuminates due to a drop in tire air pressure, make sure to check and adjust the tire air pressures.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: ● Tires lose air naturally over time and the TPMS cannot tell if the tires are getting too soft over time or you have a flat. However, when you find one low tire in a set of four-that is an indication of trouble; you should have someone drive the vehicle slowly forward so you can inspect any low tire for cuts and any metal objects sticking through tread or sidewall. Put a few drops of water in the valve stem to see if it bubbles indicating a bad valve. Leaks need to be addressed by more than simply reinflating the tire as leaks are dangerous - take it to your Toyota dealer.

texts.orig: If  the key is left in the luggage compartment/trunk with all the doors locked and the liftgate/trunk lid closed, a beep will be heard outside for about 10 seconds to notify the driver that the key is in the luggage compartment/trunk. texts.text: This vehicle is equipped with an event data recorder (EDR). texts.label: text
texts.orig: The tread wear grade is a comparative rating based on the wear rate of the tire when tested under controlled conditions on a specified government test course.
texts.text: The tread wear grade is a comparative rating based on the wear rate of the tire when tested under controlled conditions on a specified government test course.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: For example, a tire graded 150 would wear one-and-a-half times as well on the government course as a tire graded 100.
texts.text: For example, a tire graded 150 would wear one-and-a-half times as well on the government course as a tire graded 100.

texts.label: text

texts.text: The relative performance of tires depends upon the actual conditions of  their  use,  however,  and  may  depart  significantly  from  the  norm because of variations  in  driving  habits,  service  practices  and  differences in road characteristics and climate.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The  traction  grades,  from  highest  to  lowest,  are AA, A,  B,  and  C. A  tire  marked  C  may  have  poor traction performance.

texts.orig: Driving your vehicle with under-inflated tires is dangerous.
texts.text: Driving your vehicle with under-inflated tires is dangerous.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Under-inflation is the most common cause of failures in any kind of tire and may result in severe cracking, tread separation or 'blowout', with unexpected loss of vehicle control and increased risk of injury. Underinflation  increases  sidewall  flexing  and  rolling  resistance,  resulting  in heat buildup and internal damage to the tire. It results in unnecessary tire stress, irregular wear, loss of control and accidents. A tire can lose up to half of its air pressure and not appear to be flat!
texts.text: Under-inflation is the most common cause of failures in any kind of tire and may result in severe cracking, tread separation or 'blowout', with unexpected loss of vehicle control and increased risk of injury. It results in unnecessary tire stress, irregular wear, loss of control and accidents. A tire can lose up to half of its air pressure and not appear to be flat!

Before loading your vehicle, familiarize yourself with the following terms for determining your vehicle's weight ratings, from the vehicle's Safety Certification Label and Tire and Load Information Label:

Before loading your vehicle, familiarize yourself with the following terms for determining your vehicle's weight ratings, from the vehicle's Safety Certification Label and Tire and Load Information Label:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Base Curb Weight is the weight of the vehicle including a full tank of fuel  and  all  standard  equipment.  It  does  not  include  passengers, cargo, or optional equipment.
texts.text: Base Curb Weight is the weight of the vehicle including a full tank of fuel  and  all  standard  equipment.  It  does  not  include  passengers, cargo, or optional equipment.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Vehicle  Curb  Weight  is  the  weight  of  your  new  vehicle  when  you picked it up from your dealer plus any aftermarket equipment.
texts.text: Vehicle  Curb  Weight  is  the  weight  of  your  new  vehicle  when  you picked it up from your dealer plus any aftermarket equipment.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Payload is the combination weight of cargo and passengers that the vehicle is designed to carry. The maximum payload for your vehicle can be found on the Tire and Load Information label on the driver's door frame or door pillar. Look for 'THE COMBINATION WEIGHT OF OCCUPANTS AND CARGO SHOULD NEVER EXCEED XXX kg or XXX lb.'  for  your  maximum  payload. The  payload  listed  on  the  tire label is the maximum payload for the vehicle as built by the assembly plant.  If  any  aftermarket  or  dealer  installed  equipment  has  been installed  on  the  vehicle,  the  weight  of  the  equipment  must  be  subtracted from the payload listed on the tire label in order to be accurate.

texts.label: text

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The cargo weight limit with one occupant is 849 lb. (385 kg) - 150 lb. (68 kg) = 699 lb. (317 kg)

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Overloading  a  vehicle  is  dangerous.  The  results  of  overloading  can have  serious  consequences  in  terms  of  passenger  safety.  Too  much weight  on  a  vehicle's  suspension  system  can  cause  spring  or  shock absorber failure, brake failure, handling or steering problems, irregular tire wear, tire failure or other damage.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Overloading  makes  a  vehicle  harder  to  drive  and  control.  It  also increases the distance required for stopping. In cases of serious overloading,  brakes  can  fail  completely,  particularly  on  steep  grades. The load a tire will carry safely is a combination of the size of the tire, its load range, and corresponding inflation pressure.

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Determine the combined weight of the driver and passengers that will be riding in your vehicle.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: (4) The resulting figure equals the available amount of cargo and luggage load capacity. For example, if the 'XXX' amount equals 1400 lbs.  and  there  will  be  five  150  lb  passengers  in  your  vehicle,  the amount of available  cargo  and  luggage  load  capacity  is  650  lbs. (1400 - 750 (5 x 150) = 650 lbs.)

texts.label: list_item
